data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"The safest protocol is a write-ahead undo-log with reference-counted staging directories and deterministic workspace replay; it must durably record the problem ID, sequence number, staging directory handle, pristine workspace checksum, and the promotion record.","counterconditions":[{"case":"The underlying filesystem allows partial or non-atomic promotion, exposing incomplete evidence.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"Reference count corruption causes premature staging deletion while a valid promote record exists.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"Deterministic replay from the pristine checksum fails due to undetected workspace bit-rot.","eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"The deterministic workspace is treated as a transaction. Before mutation, the process writes an undo-log entry that captures the pristine workspace checksum. Evidence is accumulated in a staging directory. To commit, the process writes a 'promote' record linking the staging handle to the final evidence path. If a crash leaves no terminal record, reclamation reads the undo-log: a 'promote' record causes the protocol to finalize the atomic rename/ref-bind even post-crash; absent that, the staging directory is discarded and the workspace is rolled back to the pristine checksum via replay. Silent displacement is impossible because the evidence path is never written in-place; it is only exposed via the durable promotion record, so a later workspace assignment cannot collide with completed evidence.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
